# Authentication

The F5 XC provider requires an API endpoint and one authentication method. The
public endpoint format is:

```text
https://<tenant>.console.ves.volterra.io/api
```

Before configuring the provider, [create the required API credential in the F5
XC Console](https://flatrender.tora.reviews/docs-v2/administration/how-tos/user-mgmt/Credentials).

Use only one credential method in a provider configuration. Set credentials in
environment variables or inject them from a CI/CD secret manager. Provider
arguments override their corresponding environment variables.

## Authentication Methods

Choose one of the following authentication methods:

| Method | Use case | Guide |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API token | Token-based automation credentials. | [API token](authentication-api-token.md) |
| API certificate | A Console-generated API certificate downloaded as a PKCS#12 bundle. | [API certificate](authentication-api-certificate.md) |

## Environment Variables

| Variable | Provider argument | Purpose |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `F5XCProvider_URL` | `url` | Required F5 XC API endpoint. |
| `F5XCProvider_API_TOKEN` | `api_token` | API-token authentication. |
| `F5XCProvider_API_P12_FILE` | `api_p12_file` | Absolute API-certificate PKCS#12 file path. |
| `VES_P12_PASSWORD` | None | Password for `api_p12_file`. |
| `F5XCProvider_TIMEOUT` | `timeout` | API timeout. Defaults to `30s`. |

## Timeout

Set `timeout` or `F5XCProvider_TIMEOUT` with a Go duration such as `"30s"`,
`"1m"`, or `"2m30s"`. The default is `"30s"`.

This timeout configures VesAPI RPC calls. It does not change the direct REST
client timeouts: API-token requests use `5s`, and API-certificate requests use
`30s`.

## Production Practices

- Use a dedicated least-privileged credential for each Terraform workload.
- Inject credentials at runtime from your CI/CD platform or secret manager.
- Rotate tokens and API certificates according to your organization policy.
- Store state in an access-controlled remote backend with encryption at rest.
- Do not set more than one authentication method; mixed credentials can produce
  ambiguous client behavior.
